s1.syndrome_frame: A toddler with a chronic skin eruption characterized by multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale, accompanied by fever and otitis media
salient_findings: Multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale
Perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm on histopathology
Scattered café au lait macules present on the back
key_facts: The eruption began 2 months previously
The patient has a history of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and juvenile xanthogranulomas
Treatment with griseofulvin and clotrimazole had not improved the rash
The patient developed fever and was diagnosed with otitis media one day prior to presentation
Current medications include acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and amoxicillin
No family history of NF1
White blood cell count is 76,400/µL
Histopathology shows perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm
Immunohistochemical staining is positive for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive immunohistochemical staining for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163, and perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm

shortlist.label: Leukemia cutis
shortlist.why_kept: High white blood cell count and perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm

shortlist.label: Juvenile xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of juvenile xanthogranulomas and the eruption is characterized by multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale

shortlist.label: Histiocytoid Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm, and positive immunohistochemical staining for CD4 and CD163

shortlist.label: Rosal-Dorfman disease
shortlist.why_kept: Positive immunohistochemical staining for CD4 and CD163, and perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm

raw.rationale: The patient's histopathology results showing perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm, along with positive immunohistochemical staining for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163, are consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis. Additionally, the patient's history of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and the presence of café au lait macules are also associated with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Leukemia cutis
rejected.why: The immunohistochemical staining pattern does not support leukemia cutis, as it is negative for CD34, CD3, and CD19, and positive for CD33 and CD123, which is more consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Juvenile xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of juvenile xanthogranuloma, the current histopathology and immunohistochemical staining results do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Histiocytoid Sweet syndrome
rejected.why: The lack of neutrophils and the presence of perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm make Histiocytoid Sweet syndrome less likely.

rejected.label: Rosal-Dorfman disease
rejected.why: The immunohistochemical staining pattern, particularly the positivity for CD33 and CD123, is not typical of Rosal-Dorfman disease, which is usually positive for S100 and CD1a.
